headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between open-webui and slim.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, MCP, and OpenAPI tool outputs, while slim reads/writes filesystem artifacts and runs shell commands. If slim-produced content is surfaced into open-webui through a shared workspace or copied artifacts, open-webui may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable workspace or mounted volume
IF slim writes text artifacts that open-webui later ingests as prompts or tool instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files in open-webui
Require manual review before importing slim outputs
Add provenance tags to shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches prompts, chat messages, documents, notes, files, and API keys, and has broad network egress plus cloud/API integrations. slim reads filesystem artifacts and handles registry credentials. If they share storage or credentials, either agent can expose sensitive data to the other or onward to third-party services. The profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out, so uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF the agents share a filesystem, mounted volume, or credential store
IF open-webui is configured to send file contents to external APIs
IF slim is run against images containing secrets or private keys
mitigations: Use separate secret stores for each agent
Mount only read-only inputs into slim
Disable external API connectors in open-webui for sensitive runs
Redact secrets before either agent accesses shared files
requires-engineering: isolate network egress by policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui can write to local files and mounted volumes, and slim can execute shell commands and write the filesystem. Both also have broad network egress. On a shared directory or target image, concurrent writes can overwrite artifacts or race on mutable state. The profiles do not mention locking or coordination, so conflict is plausible even though modify_git_state is absent on slim.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted directory or container image
IF open-webui writes artifacts while slim rewrites or prunes files in that path
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Run slim on copies of inputs only
Serialize access with a simple file lock
Snapshot inputs before either agent mutates them
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate prompts, documents, and tool outputs that slim may consume as command-line or file inputs, while slim performs shell execution and filesystem mutation. If slim treats open-webui output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious instruction can cascade into destructive container changes or incorrect image minimization. No verification step is documented between them.
conditions: IF open-webui output is passed directly into slim prompts, scripts, or config files
IF slim executes commands derived from open-webui text without human verification
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before execution
Require schema validation on open-webui outputs
Run slim in dry-run mode first
Compare outputs against a known-good baseline
requires-engineering: add typed interfaces between agents

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, chat messages, documents, and persistent memory, while slim handles registry credentials, certificate private keys, and vulnerability data. If the pair is used on regulated or secret-bearing workloads, their differing storage and egress patterns can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets, certificates, or personal data is processed by both agents
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the open-webui store and slim's container artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs
Set short retention on open-webui logs and memory
Delete slim artifacts after each run
Document residency and retention for both systems
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and DPA terms
